labels.tau_ps.basis: a sweep over horizons is required so conclusions are not tied to one arbitrary τ; values are cross-checked against the median transit time and the inter-crossing interval that the events step prints next to the declared τ

labels.primary_tau_ps.basis: a sweep over horizons is required so conclusions are not tied to one arbitrary τ; values are cross-checked against the median transit time and the inter-crossing interval that the events step prints next to the declared τ

events.source.basis: a single time anchor shared by both systems; the shipped gramicidin annotation is used as a cross-check — the events step prints the comparison

data.pore.crossing_cylinder_radius_A.basis: task definition: separates 'crossed through the pore' from 'crossed the bilayer past the channel'; 10 A covers the vestibules of both channels and is well under half the protein-protein spacing in the membrane

features.window_ps.basis: look-back window equals the primary horizon: dynamics are measured on the same time scale on which the prediction is made

features.mouth_radius_A.basis: two hydration shells plus the mouth vestibule; diagnostics: the dlv_entry_wide_n indicator and the fraction of frames with no permeant in the zone

model.seed.basis: a single recorded run seed; fold seeds are derived from it

model.monotone.basis: from physics, not from correlation: a wider pore cannot make a configuration less ready to pass a hydrated ion

evaluate.alarm.smooth_ps.basis: half the primary τ: smoothing stays shorter than the prediction horizon

data.stride.basis: development compute budget; the stride is part of run identity, the results folder carries it in its name; 40 ps × 4 = 160 ps between table frames

model.trees.depth_grid.basis: fixed deliberately: a 3x3x3x3 grid search showed a flat selection-criterion curve (within-fold log-loss range 0.001-0.0035 vs between-fold spread 0.094, see grid_scores in the searched run's folds.json); the criterion does not select this parameter, an edge pick would be noise rather than an optimum
